name: The Who
hook: A mod band who took the Kinks' riff, the same producer, and a drummer who refused to keep time.
blurb: Their first hit was built on purpose to sound like the Kinks, using the same producer: Shel Talmy produced both bands, and Pete Townshend has said plainly that 'I Can't Explain' was written to sound like a Kinks record. That makes them an early example of how influence in this period was often open, commercial, and arranged by a producer rather than mysterious. What made them different was Keith Moon, who played drums as constant rolling chaos instead of a steady beat, and Townshend treating feedback as something to compose with.

signatureTracks.title: I Can't Explain
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A deliberate Kinks imitation, made with the Kinks' producer, that became its own thing.

signatureTracks.title: My Generation
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Keith Moon's drumming treats the kit as a constant rolling lead part instead of a backbeat, the clearest single document of the chaos the band built its identity on.
